purpose: HTTPS services for retrieving IPFS content. Viewers offer file-response gateways whose templates need no account credentials; deployment commands do not read this catalog.

placeholders.CID: Content identifier; use CIDv1 in base32 for a subdomain URL.
placeholders.PATH: Optional path inside the CID, with each path segment URL-encoded. Omit the final slash and PATH when requesting the CID itself.
placeholders.GATEWAY_NAME: Dedicated gateway name assigned by the provider.
placeholders.GATEWAY_TOKEN: Gateway retrieval token, not a pinning or management API key.
placeholders.CLIENT_ID: thirdweb project's client ID, intended for frontend use with domain restrictions; not its secret key.

notes: IPFS.io and dweb.link are no longer ordinary HTTP retrieval options: their sponsored public gateways retired on September 21, 2026. See https://gatewaychanges.ipfs.io/ and https://blog.ipfs.tech/2026-08-beyond-sponsored-gateways/.
These are retrieval services, not publishing or pinning services. Content still needs an available provider or pin.
No authentication requirement does not mean unlimited or free hosting: storage and egress billing depend on the content provider and service plan.
Gateway authentication restricts that endpoint. It does not make publicly available IPFS content confidential or prevent retrieval through another provider.
An HTTPS gateway returning decoded JSON or a file does not by itself prove the bytes match the CID. CAM SHA-256 checks and verifiable IPFS retrieval are separate mechanisms.
Browser fetches need compatible CORS responses. A URL working in a browser tab does not establish that JavaScript on another origin can read it.
A header keeps a token out of the URL, but a token sent by browser code remains visible to that browser's user. Query tokens also appear in URLs and may reach histories or logs.
No live availability, CORS, performance, billing or service-level guarantee is asserted by this catalog. Consult the provider's current account settings and terms.

trustless-gateway-link.name: IPFS Foundation verifiable-response gateway
trustless-gateway-link.contentScope: Verifiable CAR streams, raw blocks and IPNS records; not decoded JSON or image responses.
trustless-gateway-link.notes: Requires a client that verifies and decodes the returned IPFS blocks. A plain JSON fetch cannot use this template directly.

filebase-public.name: Filebase public
filebase-public.notes: Shared gateway intended for testing and light usage; rate-limited. Filebase recommends a dedicated gateway for production traffic.

pinata-public.name: Pinata public
pinata-public.contentScope: Public IPFS content available through the gateway.
pinata-public.notes: Shared public endpoint; account-based dedicated gateways are listed separately. Documentation review does not establish current availability or an uptime guarantee.

pinata-dedicated.name: Pinata dedicated gateway
pinata-dedicated.authentication: For token-based access, supply a gateway token using the header or query alternative below. Configured IP or origin rules can also admit requests. This is not the Pinata API JWT.
pinata-dedicated.contentScope: Defaults to content pinned to the account. Retrieval from the wider IPFS network requires appropriate gateway access controls.
pinata-dedicated.notes: Provision a dedicated gateway first. Account, origin and IP restrictions affect which requests are accepted; possessing a CID is not sufficient for every gateway configuration.

filebase-dedicated.name: Filebase dedicated gateway
filebase-dedicated.authentication: Configurable. A token-protected gateway requires its retrieval token using the header or query alternative below. Do not substitute an S3 access key or secret.
filebase-dedicated.contentScope: Depends on gateway configuration: account-pinned content or selected CIDs can be enforced.
filebase-dedicated.notes: Provision the gateway and create its tokens in the Filebase dashboard. Public and restricted configurations have different retrieval scope.

thirdweb.name: thirdweb project gateway
thirdweb.authentication: Project client ID in the hostname, subject to the project's API-key domain restrictions. A client ID is publishable; a backend secret key is not.
thirdweb.contentScope: IPFS retrieval through the project's Storage service.
thirdweb.notes: Enable and configure Storage for the project. This is the browser URL form documented for resolveScheme; use the documented SDK client for backend secret-key authentication rather than putting a secret in the URL.
